newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed lower across the board on Monday in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly across the board following a hike in the volatile interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.63/98.68 compared with last Friday's close of S$98.75/98.80, May 2002 at S$99.53/99.58 against S$99.63/99.68 and June 2003 at S$94.58//94.63 from S$94.75/94.80.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 4-1/4 4 percent versus last Friday's 2-3/4 2-5/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.60/2.55 percent against last Friday's yield of 2.40/2.35 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.61/2.56 percent from 2.55/2.50 percent.
